findings.title: Release proposal bypasses capture-loss handling
findings.message: On MouseUp the resize is queued unconditionally, even if the pointer was never moved or capture was lost. Resize is only suppressed later by the width-equality check in ui. A cancelled capture may still produce a proposal at release, and queue is called without the guard used for the move path.
findings.suggestion: Make sure the MouseUp proposal is skipped when capture was cancelled, and confirm that queue applies the same validity and disabled checks as the move path.

findings.title: Fragile slice aliasing when inserting sort chevron
findings.message: The inner append builds a new slice from children[1:] before the outer append writes into children[:1]'s backing array, which is safe only by accident. The code also mutates children[0].Text through the shared slice and relies on aliasing with headers' last element. This pattern is fragile and hard to reason about.
findings.suggestion: Build the new children slice explicitly: nc := []Node{children[0], chevron}; nc = append(nc, children[1:]...); then assign it to headers[len(headers)-1].Children.
